title: Masala omelette
summary: Five minutes, one pan, 20 g of protein. The one thing worth getting right is keeping the heat low enough that it stays soft.
steps: Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper until the whites and yolks are completely combined - 20 seconds of real effort, not five half-hearted stirs.
Stir in the onion, tomato, chilli, coriander and spices.
Heat the oil in a small pan over medium-low. Low heat is the entire secret to a tender omelette.
Pour in the mixture. As it sets at the edges, drag them into the centre with a spatula and tilt the pan so the raw egg runs into the gap.
When the top is nearly set but still glossy, add the cheese if using, fold in half, and give it 30 seconds more.
Slide it out. The centre should still be just slightly soft.
tips: Salting the eggs a couple of minutes before cooking makes them noticeably more tender.
Deseed the tomato or it weeps water and the omelette will not set properly.
Two eggs plus two whites gets you the same protein for about 60 fewer calories.
health_notes: Whole eggs are worth eating - the yolk carries the choline, the vitamin D and most of the micronutrients. This is roughly 20 g of complete protein for under 300 calories.

source.adapted: Standard Indian omelette, cooked in a teaspoon of oil on low heat.
